1.name: ABRASIVE
1.description: Removing unwanted tissue or foreign materials from various body surfaces, including mechanical tooth cleaning and/or gloss improvement.

2.name: ABSORBENT
2.description: Taking up water- and/or oil-soluble (dissolved or finely dispersed) substances.

4.name: ANTI-SEBORRHEIC
4.description: Preventing or relieving the symptoms of seborrhea and/or seborrheic dermatitis, including dandruff.

6.name: ANTICAKING
6.description: Preventing agglomeration of particulate solids into lumps or hard masses (cohesive cake), thus allowing free flow of particles.

7.name: ANTICORROSIVE
7.description: Preventing and or inhibiting the corrosion of the packaging material.

8.name: ANTIFOAMING
8.description: Suppressing foam during manufacturing or reducing the tendency of finished products to generate foam.

9.name: ANTIMICROBIAL
9.description: Preventing and/or slowing down microbial growth.

10.name: ANTIOXIDANT
10.description: Inhibiting reactions promoted by oxygen, thus avoiding oxidation and rancidity.

13.name: ANTISTATIC
13.description: Preventing and/or reducing static electricity by neutralising electrical charge on surfaces.

15.name: BINDING
15.description: Providing adhesive properties during and after compression in cosmetic tablets and/or cakes.

16.name: BLEACHING
16.description: Bleaching or lightening the shade of hair and/or skin.

17.name: BUFFERING
17.description: Stabilising the pH of an aqueous medium in a narrow range even if an acid or base is added. Altering and/or maintaining a cosmetic product's pH at the desired level.

18.name: BULKING
18.description: Non-reactive (chemically inert), solid ingredients that dilute other solids and/or  increase the volume of cosmetic products.

19.name: CHELATING
19.description: Forming complexes with metal ions which could affect the stability and/or appearance of cosmetics.

20.name: CLEANSING
20.description: Helping to keep the body surface clean.

21.name: COLORANT
21.description: Exclusively or mainly intended to colour the cosmetic product, the body as a whole or certain parts thereof, by absorption or reflection of visible light; (precursors of oxidative hair colorants shall be deemed colorants). All authorised colorants are substances in the positive list of Annex IV to the Cosmetics Regulation 1223/2009.

22.name: DENATURANT
22.description: Rendering cosmetics unpalatable. Mostly added to cosmetics containing ethyl alcohol to make it unsuitable for ingestion.

23.name: DEODORANT
23.description: Reducing and/or eluminating unpleasant odour. Contributing against the formation of malodour on body surfaces.

24.name: DEPILATORY
24.description: Breaking down the the mechanical strength of hair fibers so that they can be removed by mild scraping/rubbing.

25.name: DETANGLING
25.description: Reducing or eliminating hair intertwining due to hair surface alteration or damage and, thus, helping combing.

26.name: DISPERSING NON-SURFACTANT
26.description: Facilitating the dispersion of solids in liquids. They function primarily by coating the solid through the process of adsorption, thus changing the surface characteristic of the suspended solid.

27.name: EMULSION STABILISING
27.description: Helping the process of emulsification and improving emulsion stability and shelf-life.

28.name: EPILATING
28.description: Applied to the skin, and stripped off quickly to remove hair. With epilation the entire hair is removed from the follicle, whereas with depilation the hair is removed only to the surface of the skin.

29.name: EXFOLIATING
29.description: Initiating and/or accelerating removal of the layers of dead skin cells from the skin surface.

30.name: EYELASH CONDITIONING
30.description: Conditioning and enhancing the appearance of eyelashes. Improving the gloss or sheen of eyelashes, coating the eyelash hair to increase the appearance of its diameter and length, or helping with the separation of the eyelash hair.

31.name: FILM FORMING
31.description: Producing (upon application) a continuous film on the skin, hair or nails.

32.name: FLAVOURING
32.description: Imparting taste and/or flavour to a cosmetic product.

33.name: FOAMING
33.description: Traping numerous small bubbles of air or other gas within a small volume of liquid by modifying the surface tension of the liquid.

34.name: FRAGRANCE
34.description: Imparting an odour or taste. Creating a perceivable pleasant smell and/or masking a bad smell.

35.name: GEL FORMING
35.description: Giving the consistency of a gel (a semi-solid preparation with some elasticity) to a liquid preparation.

36.name: HAIR CONDITIONING
36.description: Enhancing the appearance and feel of hair. Leaving the hair easy to comb, supple, soft and shiny and/or imparting volume, lightness, gloss, texture, etc.

37.name: HAIR DYEING
37.description: Imparting color to hair. Hair dyeing preparations may be temporary, semi-permanent, permanent, depending on the length of time the colorant remains on the hair.

38.name: HAIR FIXING
38.description: Permitting physical control of hair style.

39.name: HAIR WAVING OR STRAIGHTENING
39.description: Modifying the chemical structure of the hair, allowing it to be set in the style required (permanent waves or hair straightening).

40.name: HUMECTANT
40.description: Retaining and/or preserving the moisture in a product during use.

41.name: KERATOLYTIC
41.description: Helping to eliminate the dead cells of the stratum corneum.

42.name: LIGHT STABILIZER
42.description: Protecting the cosmetic product from deterioration effects of light.

43.name: LYTIC
43.description: Helping to break down lipids, proteins, and polysaccharides into smaller components, usually by the action of enzymes.

44.name: MOISTURISING
44.description: Increasing the water content of the skin and keeping it soft and smooth.

45.name: NAIL CONDITIONING
45.description: Improving and/or enhancing the cosmetic characteristics of the nail (moisturizing, increasing sheen, reducing brittleness and flaking, etc.).

46.name: NAIL SCULPTING
46.description: Forming a hard structure that resembles the nail plate.

48.name: OPACIFYING
48.description: Reducing transparency or translucency of cosmetics.

49.name: ORAL CARE
49.description: Providing cosmetic effects to the oral cavity, e.g. cleansing, deodorising, protecting.

50.name: OXIDISING
50.description: Changing the chemical nature of another ingredient by adding oxygen (or removing hydrogen).

51.name: PEARLESCENT
51.description: Imparting a nacreous appearance to cosmetics.

52.name: PERFUMING
52.description: Used for perfume and aromatic raw materials.

53.name: PLASTICISER
53.description: Softening and making supple synthetic polumers that otherwise could not be easily deformed, spread or worked out.

54.name: PRESERVATIVE
54.description: Exclusively or mainly intended to inhibit the development of micro-organisms in the cosmetic product. All authorised preservatives are substances in the positive list of Annex V to the Cosmetics Regulation 1223/2009.

55.name: PROPELLANT
55.description: Generating pressure in an aerosol pack, expelling contents when the valve is opened. Some liquefied propellants can act as solvents.

56.name: REDUCING
56.description: Changing the chemical nature of another ingredient by adding hydrogen (or removing oxygen).

57.name: REFATTING
57.description: Replenishing the lipids of the hair or of the top layers of the skin.

58.name: REFRESHING
58.description: Imparting a pleasant freshness to the skin.

59.name: SKIN CONDITIONING
59.description: Maintaining the skin in good condition.

60.name: SKIN CONDITIONING - EMOLLIENT
60.description: Acting as lubricants on the skin surface providing the skin with a soft and smooth appearance.

61.name: SKIN CONDITIONING - HUMECTANT
61.description: Increasing the water content of the top layers of the skin. Humectants are primarily hygroscopic agents drawing moisture from the surrounding air.

62.name: SKIN CONDITIONING - MISCELLANEOUS
62.description: Enhancing the appearance of dry and/or damaged skin by reducing flaking and restoring suppleness.

63.name: SKIN CONDITIONING - OCCLUSIVE
63.description: Retarding the evaporation of water from the skin surface. Occlusives are generally lipids which tend to remain on the skin surface and thus increase the water content of skin.

64.name: SKIN PROTECTING
64.description: Helping to avoid harmful effects to the skin from external factors.

65.name: SLIP MODIFIER
65.description: Enhancing the flow properties of other ingredients without reacting chemically with them.

66.name: SMOOTHING
66.description: Seeking to achieve an even skin surface by decreasing roughness or irregularities.

67.name: SOLVENT
67.description: Dissolving other components of cosmetics. Solvents are usually liquids (aqueous and nonaqueous).

68.name: SOOTHING
68.description: Lightening discomfort of the skin or of the scalp.

69.name: SURFACE MODIFIER
69.description: Applied to other cosmetic components to make them more hydrophilic or hydrophobic, or to modify their physical/chemical properties (in some cases, surface modifiers may form a covalent bond with substrates).

70.name: SURFACTANT
70.description: Helping other ingredients that normally do not mix to dissolve or disperse in one another. Surfactants are also called a surface active agents as they lower the surface tension of water or reduce the interfacial tension between immiscible components.

71.name: SURFACTANT - CLEANSING
71.description: Wetting body surfaces, emulsifying or solubilizing oils, and suspending soil (generally, such ingredients contribute to the foaming and lathering properties of cleansing products).

72.name: SURFACTANT - DISPERSING
72.description: Helping distribute an insoluble solid in a liquid phase.

73.name: SURFACTANT - EMULSIFYING
73.description: Helping suspensions or dispersions of liquids in a second liquid by reducing the surface tension of the substances to be emulsified.

74.name: SURFACTANT - FOAM BOOSTING
74.description: Increasing foaming capacity and/or stabilize foams in general.

75.name: SURFACTANT - HYDROTROPE
75.description: Enhancing the water solubility of another surfactant.

76.name: SURFACTANT - SOLUBILIZING
76.description: Helping another component (solute) to dissolve in a medium in which it is not normally soluble.

77.name: TANNING
77.description: Darkening the skin with or without exposure to UV.

78.name: TONIC
78.description: Producing a feeling of well-being on skin and hair.

79.name: UV ABSORBER
79.description: Protecting the cosmetic product from the effects of UV-light.

80.name: UV FILTER
80.description: Exclusively or mainly intended to protect the skin and/or hair against certain UV radiation by absorbing, reflecting or scattering UV radiation. All authorised UV filters are substances in the positive list of Annex VI to the Cosmetics Regulation 1223/2009.

81.name: VISCOSITY CONTROLLING
81.description: Increasing or decreasing the viscosity (thickness) of cosmetics.

82.name: pH ADJUSTERS
82.description: Controlling the pH of cosmetic products.
